fields.title: 1. Event ① — $40 Billion GPU Lease Syndication: Reports vs. Source Text vs. Filings
fields.md:
| Date (US) | Fact | Source grade · source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-24 / 10-26 | **8-K Item 8.01** (baseline): master financial lease commitment letter signed with an Apollo-managed entity — "aggregate principal payments … approximately $40 billion" · about 5 to 5.25 years per tranche · quarterly advance rent = 1/20 of each tranche's financing cost + **"fixed rate per annum" (fixed at pricing)** + operating expenses · "subject to certain specified closing conditions" · "expected to close prior to year end" · "lease schedules are expected to commence during the first half of 2027 upon delivery of the GPUs". **No mention of prepayment, lessor-side loans/bonds, PIMCO, syndication, or total hardware amount** | ① [8-K 10/26](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000110465926118614/tm2628247d1_8k.htm), re-read 2026-11-05 |
| 2026-10-26 | IR press release: led by Apollo and Goldman, Nvidia Vera Rubin, anchors BlackRock, GSAM and KKR advisory accounts (recorded in the 10/27 round) | ② [IR 10/26](https://ir.spacex.com/updates/releases-details/2026/SPACEX-SECURES-40-BILLION-IN-THE-LARGEST-GPU-FINANCING-EVER-2026-EnDqGhTAB3/default.aspx) |
| **2026-11-04 (Wed)** | **Bloomberg (citing people familiar) → republished by Reuters**: Goldman Sachs and Apollo are **in talks to place part** of the roughly $40 billion financing package with investors — ahead of formal syndication, some investors were asked for advance commitments of **up to $500 million**. Reuters: "could not independently verify". Goldman declined to comment; Apollo and SpaceX did not respond immediately. The Reuters republication **does not contain $8.3 billion, $7.0 billion or $47.3 billion** | ⑤ [Reuters 11/04 (SRN republication)](https://srnnews.com/goldman-apollo-seek-buyers-for-40-billion-spacex-ai-chip-deal-bloomberg-news-reports/) · [Reuters (Investing.com republication, 16:26 ET)](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/goldman-apollo-seek-buyers-for-40-billion-spacex-ai-chip-deal-bloomberg-news-reports-5001393) · Bloomberg original: 403 for this round's tool |
| 2026-11-04 / 11-05 | **Bloomberg details (secondary republication — PANews, Phemex)**: debt package = **$8.3 billion senior secured loan (led by Goldman)** + **multiple bond tranches (Apollo as main underwriter, PIMCO participating)**; together with **$7.0 billion lease prepayment**, used for the acquisition of **about $47.3 billion of Nvidia Rubin chips**, delivery 2027-1H, 5-year lease. Interest rate, tranche sizes and closing conditions not stated. The phrase "off balance sheet" appears only in the Reuters republication (rallies.ai) | ⑥ [PANews 11/05](https://panews.io/articles/01a1a877-8025-732d-a694-7991aa27dd0e) · [Phemex 11/04 21:29](https://phemex.com/news/article/goldman-sachs-and-apollo-seek-to-sell-stakes-in-40b-spacex-ai-chip-financing-deal-102417) · [rallies.ai (citing Reuters)](https://rallies.ai/news/goldman-apollo-reportedly-seek-buyers-for-40-billion-spacex-ai-chip-deal-73baeb9b9577826a) |
| 2026-11-05 (KST) | News watcher detection (bloomberg.com · gurufocus · reuters) — **linked to T1** | `data/spacex_watch.json` due |
| Filings | **No SpaceX 8-K or IR release** — latest EDGAR item is still the 10/26 8-K (Item 8.01); latest IR RSS item is 10/26 | ① [EDGAR filing list](https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001181412.json), queried 2026-11-05 · ② [IR RSS](https://ir.spacex.com/rss/pressrelease.aspx), queried 2026-11-05 |

**Differences between sources (recorded)**: ⓐ **Structure** — 10/23 Bloomberg 'private bonds in 3 tranches (subordinated $250–300 hundred million · other $10.0 billion · additional up to $5.0 billion)' → 10/26 8-K 'lease schedule tranches · financial lease' → 11/4 Bloomberg 'senior secured loan $8.3 billion + multiple bonds'. The three descriptions are **at different layers** — the 8-K describes the lease between SpaceX (lessee) and the lessor, while Bloomberg describes how the lessor (the Apollo-managed entity) raises the money to acquire the chips. They complement rather than contradict one another, but the lessor-side figures are not subject to SpaceX disclosure, so **a source text may never exist** ⓑ **Total** — $47.3 billion − $7.0 billion prepayment = $40.3 billion ≠ 'about $40 billion' (the 8-K's figure is 'aggregate principal payments of about $40 billion', while Bloomberg's $47.3 billion is the chip acquisition amount, so the definitions differ — neither is adopted or back-calculated) ⓒ **'8.3'** — Semafor 10/22's 'bottom 8.3%' is an interest rate, while Bloomberg 11/4's '$8.3 billion' is a loan size. The same number denotes different quantities — do not confuse them ⓓ **FT 10/06 'bank loan $10.0 billion + IG bonds $30.0 billion'** and 11/4 'loan $8.3 billion + bonds' read as adjusted versions of the same picture, but the FT original has not been re-verified (sources: table above · `reports/2026-10-27-event.md` · `state.triggers_next_12m[T5].note`).

**Confirmed as fact**: ① Bloomberg reported syndication talks on 11/4 and Reuters republished it (the fact extends only to 'a report was made') ② No official confirmation from SpaceX, Apollo or Goldman ③ The 8-K states that the fixed rate is set at 'pricing' before closing — syndication is the usual procedure at that stage. **Unconfirmed**: $8.3 billion · $7.0 billion · $47.3 billion · PIMCO · loan/bond split (Bloomberg original not read, secondary republication) · fixed rate · payer and timing of the $7.0 billion prepayment (if SpaceX pays it in 2026, it comes out of liquidity of $89.86 billion — 10-Q as of 9/30, `state.latest_reported_quarter`) · closing date (sources: table above).
